aliases.name: M38 Squad Designated Marksman Rifle
aliases.note: An M27 with a variable-power optic and a suppressor, issued one per squad.

massEmpty.sourceNote: 7.9 lb empty. The article gives 9.8 lb loaded with a sling, so this figure is the bare rifle.

length.sourceNote: 36.9 in, the adjustable stock at its longest setting.

lengthFolded.sourceNote: 33 in, the adjustable stock fully collapsed. The stock telescopes rather than folding.

barrelLength.sourceNote: 16.5 in, the standard barrel. A shorter 11 in barrel is issued for the Reconnaissance Weapons Kit.

cyclicRate.sourceNote: The article gives a cyclic range of 700 to 900 rounds a minute; the midpoint of that range is recorded here because a PropertyValue holds one number. The sustained rate is given separately as 36 rounds a minute.

effectiveRange.sourceNote: Effective range against a point target. The same source gives 700 m against an area target.

productionTotal.sourceNote: The number of rifles the Marine Corps had bought as of April 2019, not a lifetime production figure.

launchPrice.sourceNote: Unit cost to the Marine Corps under the 2018 contract. This is a government procurement price, not a retail one.

capacity.sourceNote: STANAG magazine. The programme's original requirement asked for at least 100 rounds and was changed to the standard 30-round magazine.

images.alt: An M27 rifle seen from the left against a plain ground. It has a black telescoping stock, an AR-pattern pistol grip and lower receiver marked Heckler & Koch, a long railed handguard with a vertical foregrip at the front, a folding rear sight on the receiver rail, a curved thirty-round magazine and a flash hider at the muzzle. A blue chamber flag hangs from the ejection port.
images.caption: An M27 with a vertical foregrip and its iron sights folded up, shown with a chamber safety flag fitted. The receiver markings read Heckler & Koch GmbH, Made in Germany, and Heckler & Koch Defense Inc., Ashburn VA.

images.alt: A line of Marines in desert camouflage firing rifles upward from the deck of a ship, the nearest one holding an M27 by a magwell grip with a red-dot sight on the rail and smoke drifting from the muzzle. The ship's superstructure and grey sea fill the background.
images.caption: Marines of the 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit firing M27s from the deck of USS Boxer in August 2026. The rifles carry a squad day optic on the receiver rail and are gripped at the magazine well rather than by a foregrip.
